newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude seen sideways, may test lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude seen sideways, may test lower.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
---------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - JULY 22 --------------
* A test of the lower end of the range is favoured at some point today for NYMEX crude but there is no point getting too bearish while the support levels hold, aanalysts said.
* A succession of lower highs and lower lows continues to confirm the market in longer term downtrend.

NYMEX crude and product futures are expected to continue trading sideways on Tuesday with momentum indicators mildly supportive while a longer term downtrend appears intact, fuelling bearish forward sentiment, analysts said.

Analysts said as with Brent, NYMEX crude appears to be trading into the apex of a bearish pennant formation formed by a long term downtrend line stemming from December 19's $26.80 high and a more recent uptrend line from June 20's $18.35 low on the spot month chart.
The market more recently has been bouncing off the supportive uptrend line but analysts said any break through this support could tip the market lower.
A more recent line down from down May 16's $22.40 high which capped gains last week at $19.76 remains in place.
On the September chart slow stochastics crossed on Friday and Monday's near Doji day on the candlestick chart both flagged that the recent small rally has ended.
However, despite more bearish medium term indicators, analysts remained optimistic for the nearby market while supports continue to hold, though longer term bearishness rules.
Darren Gurner at Sucden said "the succession of lower highs and lower lows continues to confirm the market in longer term downtrend."
He expected resistance on the September chart to hold around $20.50 with short term support at $19.25, $19.13, $19 and $18.80 before the low of $18.50 from last week is tested.
"It may not happen this week but certainly next week people will be looking in that area," Gurner said.
GNI Research said in a report, "A test of the lower end of the range is favoured at some point today but there is no point getting too bearish while the various support levels hold".
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International said "On Tuesday look for the price to probe the $19.62-86 neighbourhood, then roll back to under $19.25".
He said the bigger picture was open to multiple interpretation but generally expected weakness to resume.
Gasoline bounced off uptrend support at around 58.85 cents on Monday to form a long legged Doji candles stick on the spot month chart.
According to Japanese candlestick charting techniques this reflects an irresolute market that has lost its sense of direction.
Al Graham was more positive saying, "The rise from Monday's lows looks corrective and unfinished". He looked s for prices to peak between 60.70 and 61.07 cents.

Heating oil futures were seen moving sideways with a short term downtrend line from May 16's 58.90 cent high capping any upside movement while there was little strong support to the downside before 50.70 cents.
